styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a stone/metal stairwell-down patch. Visible tones per tile are 9 against 3 and 6 for the references. Near-flat coverage is 0%, matching tatami and below flooring's 2%. Only 24% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline mostly leans toward the cool grey-blue of the adjacent material rather than being a uniform black sticker line. The step treads and frame show banding and highlight edges rather than large single-colour areas. It is slightly more graphic than the grain-heavy floor references, but it is not thinner or flatter than them.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a grey stone stairwell with a metal grate and an ember glow, not a ground surface patch like the flooring and tatami references. Its structure differs from them, so the kind comparison is only partial. On the measured facts it is at or above the references: 9 visible tones per tile against 3 (flooring) and 6 (tatami), 0% near-flat coverage, and no 5x5 flat fills. Shading has roughly 5 steps on the stone frame and grate, against about 3-6 on the references. The outline is a dark edge around the frame, only 24% near-neutral, so it leans toward a tinted tone but is partly neutral, which I call mixed. Texture is present as grate bars and a lit interior, but there is no grain on the stone, so I rate it 'some'. The piece is not a floor patch at all, and it is drawn at a size that doesn't fit a 4x3 ground layout. Because the kind does not match the reference, the comparison can't confirm it is acceptable as a ground patch.
